description: Comprehensive map of tender portals, active procurement entities, named municipalities, and typical contract structures for government-funded community Wi-Fi and broadband deployments in South Africa.
enhancements_over_previous_version: Added named active tenders with reference numbers (Nelson Mandela Bay SCM/1356/G/2025-2026, eThekwini 34151-1i)
Added SITA as a major procurement entity with gCommerce portal
Added City of Tshwane, Johannesburg, Cape Town, Ekurhuleni, Buffalo City as named entities
Added CSD registration as mandatory compliance requirement
Added Government Printing Works tender bulletin URL
Added SAP Ariba / gCommerce procurement platforms
Expanded contract structure with SLA performance metrics and disqualification risks
Added PPPFA scoring system (80/20 and 90/10) detail
Added ICT Sector Code BBBEE compliance requirement

tender_portals.name: eTenders — National Treasury
tender_portals.notes: Primary official South African government tender portal. Lists all national, provincial, SOE, and municipal tenders. Filter by 'Telecommunications', 'IT Networking', or 'Broadband'. Monitor daily — published every business day.
tender_portals.alert_tip: Set keyword alerts for: Wi-Fi, hotspot, broadband, connectivity, WAN, LAN, network infrastructure, ICT.

tender_portals.name: Government Tender Bulletin (GPW)
tender_portals.notes: Published every Friday by Government Printing Works. Official gazette for consolidated tender notices across all South African government spheres. Useful for catching tenders missed on eTenders.
tender_portals.alert_tip: Download the weekly PDF and search for 'wireless', 'Wi-Fi', 'hotspot', 'connectivity'.

tender_portals.name: SITA — State Information Technology Agency
tender_portals.notes: Manages government-wide IT procurement. Issues LAN, WAN, Wi-Fi, and broadband RFBs/RFQs on behalf of national and provincial departments including Basic Education, Health, Home Affairs. Requires supplier accreditation under SITA transversal contracts (e.g. RFB 1183 for networking services).
tender_portals.alert_tip: Monitor SITA Invitations page and register on gCommerce (https://ww1.gcommerce.gov.za) to bid on SITA-managed tenders.

tender_portals.name: gCommerce (National Treasury e-Procurement)
tender_portals.notes: Electronic bid submission platform used by SITA and City of Tshwane. Required for submitting bids on many national connectivity tenders. Separate registration from eTenders — must register as supplier before bidding.
tender_portals.alert_tip: Pre-register before any tender deadline. Compulsory for SITA-managed connectivity bids.

tender_portals.name: Tender Bulletins
tender_portals.notes: Aggregates SA government tenders in Telecommunications, Broadcasting and Wi-Fi category. Covers national departments, provinces, SOEs. Useful complement to eTenders for catching overlooked notices.

tender_portals.name: TenderAlerts
tender_portals.notes: Alert-based subscription service for IT networking and telecommunications tenders across South Africa. Sends email notifications for new matching tenders.

tender_portals.name: OnlineTenders
tender_portals.notes: Broad aggregator for IT and Telecoms tenders from all South African government bodies.

tender_portals.name: EasyTenders
tender_portals.notes: Technology and Telecommunications tender aggregator. Provides filtering by keyword and region.

tender_portals.name: TendersOnTime
tender_portals.notes: South Africa telecom tenders, bids and RFPs — both government and SOE connectivity. Searchable by category and province.

active_procurement_entities.procurement_type: Provisioning (design, supply and installation) of ICT wireless infrastructure. Closing date: 30 July 2026.
active_procurement_entities.notes: Also issued SCM/1353/G/2025-2026 for ICT UTP cabling infrastructure (same closing date). Both tenders open simultaneously — indicative of a broader ICT infrastructure upgrade cycle.

active_procurement_entities.procurement_type: Wholesaling of excess network capacity on eThekwini Municipality Carrier Grade Network — 36-month period. Closing: 24 July 2026. Also active: supply and delivery of Wi-Fi 7 access points (Ref: BS 750).
active_procurement_entities.notes: eThekwini has a dedicated Smart City Office. Active infrastructure procurement includes both carrier-grade network capacity and Wi-Fi 7 hardware — signals significant connectivity upgrade cycle.

active_procurement_entities.procurement_type: Appointment of service providers for ICT services, corporate network infrastructure maintenance, and business application support.
active_procurement_entities.notes: Tshwane uses SAP Ariba Business Network for e-tendering. Suppliers must register on gCommerce before bidding. Monitor ICT and Infrastructure categories on Tshwane tender portal.

active_procurement_entities.entity: City of Johannesburg (incl. Metropolitan Trading Company — MTC)
active_procurement_entities.procurement_type: Enterprise connectivity services, telecommunications infrastructure, public Wi-Fi in CBD and township areas. MTC manages public Wi-Fi hotspot contracts for the CoJ.
active_procurement_entities.notes: The Metropolitan Trading Company (MTC) — a CoJ entity — has historically managed public Wi-Fi hotspot rollouts in Johannesburg. Monitor both CoJ tenders portal and MTC directly.

active_procurement_entities.procurement_type: Telecommunications infrastructure, Wi-Fi solution maintenance, smart city ICT rollouts. Issues RFIs for smart technologies before formal RFP phase.
active_procurement_entities.notes: 3rd in Africa IMD Smart City Index (2026). Regular ICT and Telecommunications tenders. Bidders must register on City supplier database. Cape Town runs SmartCape Wi-Fi network across libraries — ongoing managed service contract.

active_procurement_entities.procurement_type: ICT and smart city infrastructure. Active bids visible under ICT and Infrastructure categories.
active_procurement_entities.notes: Ekurhuleni runs own municipal Wi-Fi initiatives. Monitor Open Tenders portal for ICT hardware, network, and Wi-Fi-related RFPs and RFQs.

active_procurement_entities.procurement_type: Public Wi-Fi hotspots (historic: Quigney, Southernwood); future ICT and smart city connectivity projects.
active_procurement_entities.notes: Buffalo City has documented smart city and public Wi-Fi goals. Monitor Formal Tenders and RFQ sections under ICT/Infrastructure.

active_procurement_entities.entity: National Dept of Communications and Digital Technologies (DCDT)
active_procurement_entities.procurement_type: 32,055 community Wi-Fi hotspots and household connectivity by 2026. Covers 18,520 schools, 5,731 healthcare facilities, 949 libraries and Thusong centres, 567 SAPS sites, 8,241 tribal authorities.
active_procurement_entities.notes: Largest single connectivity procurement programme in SA. ISPs contracted as implementation partners and managed service providers. Funded via USAF and DCDT budget.

active_procurement_entities.entity: USAASA / Universal Service and Access Fund (USAF)
active_procurement_entities.tender_reference: Ongoing — R173 million digital inclusion fund FY2025/26
active_procurement_entities.procurement_type: Grant and subsidy mechanism for ICT connectivity in unconnected and underserved communities. Draft USAF administration manual gazetted February 2026 — establishes subsidy and project grant distribution framework.
active_procurement_entities.notes: ISPs can apply directly for USAF project grants. Parliament flagged recurring implementation delays and unspent allocations — watch for catch-up procurement cycles.

active_procurement_entities.procurement_type: Supply, installation, commissioning and maintenance of scalable fibre internet services — 3-year contract (July 2025 to June 2028).
active_procurement_entities.notes: Example of a small municipality issuing multi-year connectivity service contract. Pattern repeats across Garden Route and Southern Cape municipalities.

active_procurement_entities.procurement_type: Fibre optic network maintenance and minor project work on as-required 3-year contracts.
active_procurement_entities.notes: BBI has connected 3,401 public Wi-Fi hotspots (April 2023–March 2025). Ongoing maintenance and expansion contracts for ISP partners and infrastructure suppliers.

contract_structures.detail: 3–5 year contracts with monthly recurring revenue (MRR) model. Most common structure for municipal and SOE connectivity deployments.
contract_structures.notes: Contracts awarded in 2022–2023 are entering renewal/re-tender phase in 2025–2026 — primary sales window.

contract_structures.detail: Availability typically specified at 99.5%+ uptime. SLI (Service Level Indicator) credits applied if performance falls below threshold. Minimum speeds often specified (e.g. 5 Mbps per community hotspot). Incident response timeframes mandated.
contract_structures.notes: Penalties can include financial deductions and contract termination for persistent non-compliance.

contract_structures.detail: Mandatory for all government tenders. Evaluated under PPPFA using 80/20 points system (contracts under R50 million) or 90/10 (contracts R50 million+). ICT Sector Code BBBEE contributor level (1–8) determines preference points. Minimum Level 2 or higher commonly required for maximum preference scoring.
contract_structures.notes: Sub-contracting to qualifying SMMEs and Black-owned businesses can improve BBBEE score.

contract_structures.detail: ISPs must hold valid ECS (Electronic Communications Service) and/or ECNS (Electronic Communications Network Service) licence to bid on infrastructure and broadband service contracts.
contract_structures.notes: Class licences (C-ECS/C-ECNS) sufficient for most regional contracts. Individual licences required for national or large-scale projects.

contract_structures.detail: All bidders must be registered on the National Treasury Central Supplier Database (CSD) before submitting any government bid.
contract_structures.notes: Registration at https://secure.csd.gov.za. Verify your CSD status is active — expired registrations cause disqualification.

contract_structures.detail: Most ICT infrastructure tenders require compulsory attendance at a pre-bid briefing session. Non-attendance results in automatic disqualification regardless of bid quality.
contract_structures.notes: Check every tender document for briefing session dates as soon as a relevant tender is identified.

contract_structures.detail: Common for public-space and community hotspot deployments. ISP provides end-to-end: hardware (APs, routers, switches), backhaul, captive portal, bandwidth management, and ongoing maintenance under a single contract.
contract_structures.notes: OEM authorisation letters from hardware manufacturers (e.g. Cisco, Mikrotik, Ubiquiti, Huawei) may be required as part of the bid.

contract_structures.detail: For monetised public hotspots (e.g. taxi ranks, malls, CBD areas). Municipality or venue owner receives a share of advertising or voucher revenue. ISP earns from data sales and advertising. Requires POPIA-compliant captive portal.
contract_structures.notes: Less common in pure government contracts; more prevalent in PPP (public-private partnership) arrangements.

mandatory_registrations: ICASA ECS or ECNS Licence — https://www.icasa.org.za
BBBEE Certificate (ICT Sector Code) — from SANAS-accredited verification agency
SITA Supplier Accreditation — for SITA-managed tenders (https://www.sita.co.za)
gCommerce registration — for Tshwane, national departments using SAP Ariba (https://ww1.gcommerce.gov.za)
optional_but_advantageous: POPIA compliance attestation from appointed Information Officer
OEM partnership letters (Cisco Meraki, Ubiquiti, Mikrotik, etc.)
